summary: LightCraft is a free photo library and photo editor, like Adobe Lightroom. It keeps your photos in a library that you can browse. You can adjust light and colour. Your edits never change the original file.
use_cases: Apply 1 saved set of settings to all photos from a trip. Then adjust the few photos that need more work.
Join 3 photos of a sunset (dark, normal and bright) into 1 photo. The bright sky and the dark shore both keep their detail.
Export small copies for the web with your name or a caption in the corner.
Save your settings. Next month, apply them again to make the new photos match.
story: LightCraft made the cover photo of the project. It joined 3 photos of a computer-made sunset (dark, normal and bright) into 1 photo. Then it gave the photo warm orange colours, more contrast and darker corners for the cover. A small caption in the corner says that the scene is invented. LightCraft also supplied the sample photos that PhotoCraft used.
recipe: lightcraft-cli merge hdr dark.dng normal.dng bright.dng
lightcraft-cli render cover-HDR.dng -o cover.jpg --preset lc.teal-orange --set light.contrast=30
recipe_note: Join 3 photos (dark, normal and bright) into 1 photo. Export it with a saved set of settings and 1 more change. Save a picture of the library screen.

headless_notes: render, merge, synth-merge, run --demo app.export and snapshot all ran without a window. The docs say that snapshot draws the full interface on the CPU, with no window and no GPU. A snapshot took about 1 second. app.export with a folder path wrote to the working folder, so the steps use a file path. The synthetic panorama preview had a visible seam, so the page does not use it. All source images are synthetic. The project uses no real photographs.
